Advent Calendar Day 1
Happy Holidays Everyone!
Welcome to the first day of the 2023 Advent Calendar. Christmas holds a truly special place in my heart. It's a time of year that we can all celebrate the things that truly matter.
The spirit of giving also resonates deeply with me during Christmas and although I have never really considered myself all that great at creating resources, (I am more of an editor really), I do enjoy the process, and am inspired by those who every year release an Advent Calendar.
With all that said, I hope there are those who can find some use for the resources I have made and I hope everyone has a blessed holiday season!
I'm starting off the Adent with an SV Battler of the MZ Monster_7. Ever since I first saw the character sprite of this monster, I knew I wanted to use him as a major villain in my game. I went about trying to create an SV Battler using the full body image as a base. It was sized to match the other sprites I was using. In my game I don't have this character perform a physical attack so originally I didn't animate one but I figure I should have at least one physical attack if I am going to release this to the public so I created and included it in the sprite sheet. For the physical attack motion wave, I used part of one of Vibratos attack waves and edited it to match, so please remember to include him in the credits. Personally I think he works better just casting spells at the party but to each their own.
I included one sheet with the shadows, (I've always felt floating characters work better with the shadows included), and one sprite sheet without for those who wish to have it either way.
Monster_7

Advent Calendar Day 21
Today's Advent Calendar brings us Day 1 of 2 involving MegaMan.
MegaMan, also known as Rockman in Japan, is a beloved video game franchise created by Capcom. The series follows our robotic hero as he battles against various evil robots and their creator, Dr. Wily.
I have often felt that because of it's iconic pixel art style, MegaMan could seamlessly be converted to the RPG Maker style. By leveraging RPG Maker's unique mechanics, players could experience a narrative-driven adventure that explores MegaMan's relationships with allies like Roll and Dr. Light, as well as the motivations of his foes. The turn-based combat system could introduce strategic elements, allowing players to utilize various abilities acquired from defeated Robot Masters. Additionally, customizable character progression and side quests could enhance the gameplay experience, creating a fresh take on the classic franchise while retaining its iconic charm.
The possibilities are out there...

You can't use copyrighted material in anything you distribute, regardless of whether it's commercial or not. It's all a violation of copyright.
Your advantage in this particular case is that it's not an exact recreation of the original sprite, and - to me, at least - the RPG Maker chibi version certainly is recognizable if you say "this is Megaman," but it wouldn't have been the first thing I thought of when I looked at it. But using it and calling it that - all fan games are technically violations of copyright, unless a given company has explicitly given permission for them.
